newsitem.title: USA: Producer edges out stars in Grammy nominations.
newsitem.headline: Producer edges out stars in Grammy nominations.

text.p: While such major stars as Hootie and the Blowfish, Michael Jackson and Pearl Jam went emptyhanded, a pop music producer walked off with the most nominations on Tuesday for this year's Grammy awards.

In a year when the producer seemed to be eclipsing the artist, 38-year-old Kenneth "Babyface" Edmonds racked up 12 nominations, including ones in the best record, best album and best song of the year categories. His showing tied the all-time record for nominations set by Michael Jackson 14 years ago for his "Thriller" project.

Eleven of Babyface's nominations went for records and albums he produced -- most notably Eric Clapton's "Change the World" record and the "Waiting to Exhale" soundtrack featuring Whitney Houston -- or for songs he wrote. But he was also nominated in one performance category -- best R&B performance by a duo or vocal group.
The rock group Smashing Pumpkins was second in nominations with seven, while singer-songwriter Tracy Chapman and country artist Vince Gill tied for third with five nominations each.

Tied for fourth with four nominations apiece were rock star Eric Clapton, French-Canadian pop singer Celine Dion, producer David Foster, French classical conductor Pierre Boulez and R&B artist Tony Rich.

While some pop stars missed the Grammys boat, the Beatles and Frank Sinatra were not forgotten. The Beatles, who broke up in 1970, years before many of today's music fans were born, were nominated for best pop performance by a duo or group for "Free As A Bird," a song not released until last year.
Sinatra and tenor Luciano Pavarotti received a nomination in the best pop collaboration with vocals category for their performance on the "Sinatra 80th -- Live in Concert" album.

The Grammys are the music industry's version of the Oscars and its producers say it will claim an Oscar-sized audience of 1.5 billion people in 170 countries when the awards ceremony is telecast on Feb. 26 from New York's Madison Square Garden, marking the first time the Grammys have been held in a pop-concert sized arena.
A total of 450 nominations in 89 categories were made public on Tuesday morning at a ceremony attended by several pop stars -- from 72-year-old blues giant B.B. King to female singer Jewel.

The nominations for album of the year went to Beck's "Odelay," Celine Dion's "Falling Into You," Fugees' "The Score," Smashing Pumpkin's "Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness," and the soundtrack album for "Waiting to Exhale."

Vying for record of the year were Eric Clapton"s "Change the World," Tracy Chapman's "Give Me One Reason," Celine Dion's "Because You Loved Me," which was the theme from the film "Up Close and Personal," Smashing Pumpkins' "1979" and Alanis Morissette's "Ironic."
Fighting to be named the year's best new artist were Jewel, the Tony Rich project, Garbage, No Doubt and 14-year-old country singer LeAnn Rimes.
